title: Building the Brain: Development, Experience, and Neurodiversity
kicker: From Neural Progenitors to Developing Circuits and Behavior
takeaways: Neurulation, progenitor division, migration, guidance, synapse formation, myelination, and refinement overlap but require different cellular machinery.
Signals must change a concrete cellular action.
Adhesion transmits force, transporters control molecular access, and receptors regulate intracellular pathways; those actions explain how developmental changes occur.
Glia actively build and refine circuits.
Radial glia guide migration, oligodendrocytes myelinate axons, and microglia and other glia can support synapses or remove selected cellular material.
Trisomy 21, metabolic disorders, autism, and ADHD involve different and sometimes overlapping pathways; a diagnosis does not identify one uniform cellular phenotype.
Models and human findings answer different questions.
Specify the species, preparation, mutation, manipulation, and measured outcome; a cellular rescue or animal task improvement is distinct from established clinical benefit.
Development remains responsive while differences persist.
Critical periods, continued learning, metabolic management, accessible experience, and targeted supports influence trajectories without making every outcome inevitable.
